page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with one thread per core. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 3780 GB of bundled local storage and is premium storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression tests all scoring in the top 10%. Memory performance is also highly competitive; both large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks reach top-tier status, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category.

The ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX. The absence of simultaneous multithreading ensures dedicated physical execution resources per vCPU, which minimizes noisy-neighbor performance degradation. The inclusion of a large 3780 GB local disk provides high-capacity, low-latency storage directly bundled with the compute resources, reducing the need for external storage attachments for temporary data.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and top-tier database operations benchmark, this server is well-suited for database hosting, multi-threaded software compilation, and high-throughput web serving. It is also highly capable for Redis deployments, large-scale data processing, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
